assessments.subject: Brothers promise to persuade Jacob
assessments.evidence: Judah offers responsibility for Benjamin in Genesis; Qur'an 12:61 gives a brief assurance to Joseph that the brothers will seek Jacob's permission. Different speakers and moments.

assessments.subject: Joseph orders their barter goods returned
assessments.evidence: Both accounts place the payment back in the brothers' bags; Genesis explicitly mentions silver and provisions, while the Qur'an uses bidāʿa and adds Joseph's expectation that discovery will prompt return.

assessments.subject: Brothers report refusal of further grain without their brother
assessments.relationship: close narrative parallel with sequencing difference
assessments.evidence: Judah reports the Egyptian official's requirement to Jacob in Genesis 43; the Qur'an presents the brothers' collective request immediately upon return.

assessments.subject: Jacob recalls his earlier trust in the brothers and invokes divine guardianship
assessments.evidence: Both depict Jacob's reluctance and concern for Benjamin. Qur'an explicitly recalls the loss of Joseph and invokes God's superior protection; Genesis expresses grief and later reluctantly permits the journey.

assessments.subject: Returned merchandise discovered in baggage and used to persuade Jacob
assessments.evidence: Both depict the discovery of returned payment. Genesis reports discovery on the journey and again at home, with alarm and a request to return the money; Qur'an 12:65 uses the discovery as an argument for another journey and an extra camel-load.

dossier.title: Joseph, the returned payment, and Jacob's concern for Benjamin
dossier.comparative_summary: Qur'an 12:61–65 emphasizes brothers' promise, Joseph's deliberate return of their trading goods, Jacob's recollection of Joseph, and the argument for bringing Benjamin. Genesis 42:25–38 and 43:1–15 narrate returned silver, Jacob's grief, Judah's responsibility, and negotiation over Benjamin. The discovery and use of the payment differ in sequencing and rhetorical function.
dossier.transmission_caveat: Hebrew Masoretic, Greek Septuagint and Syriac Peshitta witnesses not collated. Dates of literary composition and extant manuscripts must not be conflated.
dossier.scholarly_interpretations: Compare Jewish exegetical traditions and historical-critical studies after primary texts are checked; no literary dependence inference made.
